# My thinking this year

I've been farming these 8.5 mu for a long time now, more than 30 years. I finished primary school only, so I don't do fancy calculations — I just do what worked before and watch what my neighbors do. My family has 7 mouths to feed but two of my sons work in Handan and send money home, so I'm not desperate for cash, but I still can't waste any.

Most of my land, about 6 mu, I do wheat followed by maize every year like most people in the village. It's the safest thing. I got about 450 kg/mu wheat last year and around 500 kg/mu maize — not bad, not the best. Then I have about 2 mu on the western side where the soil is a bit sandier, I plant cotton there. Cotton is more work and the price has been so-so, but my wife picks it and it gives us some cash in autumn. The last half mu I'll put in mungbean — it's quick, doesn't need much water or fertilizer, and we eat some and sell some at the market.

**Wheat** — I plant early October after the maize comes off, use the seed I bought last year (Jimai variety, the agro-store sells it). I put down about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (that's around 15 kg of N per mu) before plowing, then topdress urea at green-up in spring if the wheat looks yellow, maybe another bag across the whole field. I irrigate at over-wintering, green-up, and jointing — three times usually, the well is close so not too expensive. If it rains well in spring I skip one. Harvest around June 10.

**Maize** — Straight after wheat harvest, no time to rest the ground. I use the rotary tiller from the cooperative, costs 30 yuan/mu. Hybrid seed from the shop, Zhengdan or whatever they have. Fertilizer I put at sowing, about 20 kg compound per mu, then top-dress urea at knee-high if the leaves aren't dark green. One or two irrigations, depending on summer rain. Last year I didn't irrigate at all because it rained enough.

**Cotton** — This is the one I worry about most. Plant mid-April, use hybrid seed. Cotton needs more spraying — bollworm and aphids every year. I spend more on pesticide here than on the grain crops. Fertilize at planting and again when squaring. My wife does the picking starting in September, three or four rounds until October.

**Mungbean** — Plant end of June on the half mu near the house, harvest August. Almost no fertilizer, maybe sprinkle a bit of what's left over. No irrigation unless it's really dry. Easy crop, mostly for the family.

Labor — my wife and I do most of it, my elder brother helps at wheat harvest. We hire the combine for wheat (40 yuan/mu) and the planter for maize. Cotton picking is the most hours.
